transcript:
Header:
Date: 2026-11-18 15:00 PT
Duration: 52 minutes
Attendees: Lina Chen (Redwood AE), Marco Diaz (Redwood SE), Priya Kumar (SierraTech Lead Eng), Mark D'Souza (SierraTech PM), Jamal Reed (SierraTech Security)

Summary:
- Quick results review from last week's pilot (structured output tests + function/tool calling).
- Discussed SDK integration patterns, edge cases around tool invocation and error handling.
- Action items: provide SDK snippets, run larger synthetic test, schedule latency benchmark, share security docs.

Topics:
- SDK usage and sample code for structured output
- Function & tool calling patterns (idempotency, retries, observability)
- Error handling and malformed structured responses
- Performance tuning (batching, KV cache behavior)
- Security: KMS, audit logs, VPC considerations

Transcript Body:
[00:00] Lina: hey everyone, thanks for making time. quick roll call?
[00:05] Priya: yeah hi this is priya, i think we have mark and jamal here too.
[00:09] Mark: yep, mark here.
[00:11] Jamal: jamal on security.
[00:13] Lina: cool. marco from our side, do you want to jump into the results?
[00:17] Marco: sure. so last week we pushed the structured-output schema and ran the sanity suite against four intents. overall parsing success is at 92% for strict mode, 98% if you accept loose variations. there were two main classes of failures: one was truncated token responses — looks like a client-side timeout during streaming; the other was malformed json where the model emitted trailing commas or single quotes.
[00:42] Priya: ok that matches what we saw — a couple of cases where the app crashed when the JSON didn't parse. we added a try/catch but wanted to understand how common the malformed output is and whether you have suggestions for best practices.
[00:55] Marco: yeah common pattern is to use the SDK helper that does safety parsing, basically fallback to the 'raw_text' field and run a small sanitizer. we have a snippet in the docs: https://redwood.ai/docs/sdk#structured-output — the helper checks for trailing commas and tries a few tolerant parses before failing.
[01:12] Mark: is that in the current SDK you gave us last week? our devs looked at it but i think they were on 0.9.1.
[01:18] Lina: good call — we're sending an updated package today, 0.9.3, that includes the parse helpers and a small example of function/tool calling.
[01:25] Priya: awesome. for function calling, we had one question — when multiple tools are available, how does the runtime decide which tool to call? we want deterministic behavior.
[01:34] Marco: right, so by default we do a policy-based routing: first attempt is based on the tool confidence signal emitted by the model, then a simple routing rule you can set in the SDK: prefer local tools, or prefer lowest-latency region. you can override with explicit tool hints in the prompt. note that the model confidence isn't perfect, so we recommend a 'confirm' step for destructive actions.
[01:56] Jamal: for security we're concerned about the model calling external tools that have access to PII, how do we lock that down?
[02:03] Marco: you can scope tool permissions in the Redwood console and in the SDK you pass a tool_acl token. the runtime will reject tool calls not in the allowed list; also audit logs show the full call chain. we'll share the audit log schema.
[02:18] Priya: quick follow, does that work for private deployment or just hosted? we're running a mix: some traffic on hosted, some on our dedicated pool.
[02:26] Lina: both. the tool ACL and auditing works the same on Dedicated and Private — for Private you'll control KMS and the audit export path.
[02:34] Mark: back to performance — marco you mentioned KV cache behavior earlier in the email, can you summarize?
[02:40] Marco: sure. so the KV cache avoids re-computing past key/value states when you do conversational recency. for application integration we recommend prefix caching for commonly used prompts, and dynamic chunking for long contexts. caveat: small GPU instances can evict KV pages more aggressively, which looks like a slight bump in latency on cold starts. we saw median tok latency 10ms higher when cache evictions happened on the small instance type.
[03:09] Priya: ok makes sense — our target p95 latency is 400ms for user flows. what tuning knobs do we have to hit that?
[03:17] Marco: short list: reduce max tokens where possible, enable prefix caching for repeat prompts, set batching window to 20-40ms for background flows, and consider quantized model variants for lower cost but slightly different quality. we can run a quick benchmark against your sample traffic to give specific numbers.
[03:33] Mark: re: batching — will that cause more latency for individual interactive sessions? we worry about tail latency.
[03:40] Marco: batching trades throughput for latency; we automatically prioritize low-latency routes for interactive requests and only batch if policy allows. there's a per-route override so you can force no-batch for critical endpoints.
[03:51] Priya: perfect. we also wanted clarity on SDK integration patterns for tool/function calling in our Node backend. any sample?
[03:58] Marco: yes, sample's in the repo. snippet: initialize client, register tool handlers with a unique id, then in the response handler run response.invokeTool(toolId, payload). we added helper retries and idempotency keys in the 0.9.3 release. i'll paste the example after the call.
[04:15] Lina: (interruption) quick note — a few transcription artifacts in the recorded logs last week showed 'K-V cash' spelled wrong in a couple places, so docs might need that fix.
[04:24] Priya: ha ok noted.
[04:26] Mark: one more: structured output validation — we have a schema registry, can the SDK validate against our schema before the app consumes?
[04:33] Marco: yes, there's a schema-validate hook. you can upload your JSON schema to the console or pass it at runtime; the SDK will return a validation result with error codes. if validation fails you can either fall back to a human review or call the 'clarify' tool to ask the model to reformat.
[04:51] Priya: clarifying tool — is that something we host or you provide?
[04:54] Marco: you can register internal tools (hosted by you) or use Redwood-hosted helper tools. for internal ones the traffic stays in your VPC in Private deployment; for hosted it goes through Redwood's control plane and is subject to our data retention policy.
[05:08] Jamal: retention — what's the default for hosted? we need 30 days max and SOC2 controls.
[05:15] Lina: default is 90 days for logs, but we can configure retention per account; for enterprise customers we do 30/60/90 as required. we'll share the security pack with exact knobs.
[05:25] Mark: ok great. any regressions we noticed from last week's eval?
[05:28] Marco: besides the parsing errors and a small latency blip on cached evictions, we saw a single case where function calling looped (model kept calling same tool). that happened when the tool returned a success flag that the model misinterpreted; workaround is to include a clear 'done' signal in the tool response and add a short call-depth limit in SDK.
[05:49] Priya: good to know — we'll add done flags.
[05:51] Mark: about observability — can we get token-level cost and latency in our logs?
[05:56] Marco: yes, per-request token counts, per-stage latency (model, network, tooling), and a cost estimate are included in the request trace. in Dedicated you can export traces to your SIEM via syslog.
[06:08] Priya: great. i also wanted to ask about malformed structured output when streaming — i think our client parser fails mid-stream sometimes. any pattern?
[06:16] Marco: two patterns: 1) streaming cut-off due to timeouts — increase client read timeout or do chunk-accumulate; 2) partial JSON objects mid-stream — we suggest accumulating until the streaming 'eos' event or using the SDK's stream-sanitizer helper which tries to patch brackets. again, 0.9.3 includes that helper.
[06:35] Lina: we'll attach the sample app that shows robust streaming handling.
[06:39] Mark: outstanding question on function retries — if you have network hiccup after invoking external tool, do you retry the tool?
[06:45] Marco: SDK supports configurable retry policy. default: idempotency key required for retries on potentially non-idempotent tools, and you can set max_retries. the runtime will also detect duplicate tool calls and dedupe if idempotency is present.
[07:00] Jamal: last sec security: KMS integration — which vendors do you support?
[07:04] Marco: we support AWS KMS, GCP KMS, and HashiCorp Vault. for Private you can bring an HSM and configure the key lifecycle.
[07:13] Priya: thanks. anything on costs? we got a rough estimate last week but wanted more granular numbers for the function-calling heavy flows.
[07:20] Lina: i'll update the cost workbook with the tool-call multipliers and send it along. expect a more detailed per-10k-requests row.
[07:28] Mark: sample size — we want to run 10k synthetic messages that mimic production distribution. can you provide the runner or should we use your benchmark script?
[07:36] Marco: we have a benchmark runner and a litmus test corpus. i'll share the script and instructions; it's the one we use for latency p95 measurements.
[07:45] Priya: perfect. also, minor: our devs flagged that the SDK types for TypeScript had some mis-typed union for the tool payloads, causing compile warnings. is that fixed in 0.9.3?
[07:55] Marco: yes, fixed. we tightened the typing on tool payloads.
[07:59] Mark: any blockers from your side?
[08:01] Lina: none. we'll send the updated SDK, the sample app link, security pack, and benchmark runner.
[08:08] Priya: timeline check — we want to complete this pilot by end of month. is that feasible?
[08:13] Marco: yes, if you run the 10k test and we do the benchmark the week of 11/22, we can have preliminary numbers and follow-up by 11/29.
[08:22] Jamal: please include the audit schema and retention settings in the security pack.
[08:26] Lina: will do.
[08:28] Mark: anything else?
[08:30] Priya: no, just to confirm next steps — sdk + examples, run tests, benchmark, security docs.
[08:35] Lina: great, thanks everyone. we'll follow up via email and update the CRM notes.
